notes: Summary: Cerulean Cortex piloted Redwood Private for doc-search + automated claims triage. Initial rollout showed promise (latency and cost metrics ok), but quality regressions around structured output & tool-calling emerged mid-POC. Specifics: tool-calls sometimes returned malformed JSON or inconsistent field names (amount -> amt), causing downstream ETL failures. Quantized model variant used for cost reduction produced higher token-level hallucinations in edge cases. Customer compared to incumbent (OrchidAI) which delivered aggressive schema enforcement and deterministic tool responses. Outcome: Cerulean has moved to OrchidAI for a short-term contract; procurement is paused due to company budget freeze and the departure of their internal champion.
win_loss_notes: Closed-lost: primary reason quality regression vs incumbent on structured output and tool-calling reliability. Secondary: security wanted additional audit/logging artifacts we couldn't deliver within their compressed timeline. Tertiary: hiring/budget freeze reduced immediate spend. Customer quote (paraphrased): 'We like Redwood's cost profile, but we can't risk flaky structured outputs in production ingestion pipelines.'
decision_reasons: 1) Incumbent's deterministic schema enforcement for tool-calls. 2) Lower perceived operational risk with incumbent. 3) Cerulean paused spend (hiring freeze) and lost champion. 4) Timing: security signoff required additional deliverables we couldn't complete before their cutover window.
